column1: # id: eng205-17c-02-qa
# subject: ENG-205
# topic: Early Seventeenth Century Reading Quiz
# title: ENG-205 Early 17th Century (1603-1660) — 2 Q&A (quiz-style)
# short: 2 Q&A (quiz-style)
What event marks the beginning of the early seventeenth-century literary period?
column2: The death of Queen Elizabeth I in 1603.

column1: What was James I's title in Scotland?
column2: King James VI.

column1: What does "Jacobean" come from?
column2: Jacobus, the Latin for James.

column1: What does "Caroline" come from?
column2: Carolus, the Latin for Charles.

column1: What were the dates of James I's reign?
What did James I believe about the source of a king's power?
column2: That kings derived their power from God, not from the people.

column1: Why did James I impose illegal taxes?
column2: Because of declining Crown revenues, demand for court honors, and a costly court obsessed with feasting, drinking, and hunting.

column1: What was the Gunpowder Plot of 1605?
column2: A Catholic plan to blow up Parliament from a cellar packed with gunpowder, killing much of the ruling class.

column1: What was the most important religious event of James I's reign?
column2: His new translation of the Bible, the King James Bible.

column1: In what year did the East India Company establish England's first outpost in India?
In which church tradition was James I raised?
column2: The strict Reformed tradition of the Scottish Presbyterian Kirk, though his mother was the Catholic Mary, Queen of Scots.

column1: Why did Charles, not his older brother Henry, inherit the throne?
column2: Henry had died of typhoid fever years earlier.

column1: Who was Charles I's wife and what was her religion?
column2: The French princess Henrietta Maria, a Catholic.

column1: Whose followers were the Puritans, and what did they believe?
column2: Followers of John Calvin, who believed salvation came by faith not works and that God predestined people to be saved or damned.

column1: What did Archbishop William Laud teach about salvation?
column2: That God offered redemption freely to all, who could choose grace and work toward salvation through charity, devotion, and generosity to the church.

column1: What are the four humors?
column2: Choler, blood, phlegm, and black bile.

column1: What new discoveries began to be accepted near the end of the period?
column2: William Harvey's discovery of blood circulation and Galileo's confirmation of Copernican astronomy.

column1: Where was the small reading public for sophisticated literature concentrated?
column2: At court, the universities, and the Inns of Court (law schools).

column1: Who owned a printed work and a play script in this period?
column2: The printer owned the printed work and the theater company owned the play, not the author.

column1: When was authorial copyright first recognized?
column2: The early eighteenth century.

column1: What was Shakespeare's acting company called under James I's patronage?
column2: The King's Men.

column1: Who was the first English woman to publish a volume of original poems?
column2: Aemilia Lanyer.

column1: Who was the first English woman to publish a tragedy?
column2: Elizabeth Cary, Lady Falkland.

column1: How was William Prynne punished for attacking plays and masques in print?
column2: He lost his degrees and job, was imprisoned, had his books burned, and had his ears cut off.

column1: On what date was Charles I beheaded?
column2: 30 January 1649.

column1: What three disputed questions drove the Revolutionary Era?
column2: The ultimate source of political power, the church government laid down in Scripture, and the proper relation of church and state.

column1: How many times had Charles I dissolved Parliament by 1629?
column2: Three times.

column1: What were the dates of the First Civil War?
Where was Charles I imprisoned after the Second Civil War in 1648?
column2: The Isle of Wight.

column1: What was Cromwell's title?
column2: Lord Protector of England.

column1: Who called the "full and free" elections that led to the Restoration?
column2: General George Monck.

column1: When was Charles II proclaimed king?
When did Parliament abolish public plays?
Which two major writers sided with the republic?
column2: Andrew Marvell and John Milton.
